predictedRisks.riskTitle: Contractual misalignment may trigger commercial dispute and payment withholding
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project timeline extends 49 days beyond the September 11, 2026 contractual end date without formal amendment, creating legal ambiguity around deliverable acceptance, payment obligations, and liability coverage during the extended period through October 30, 2026.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Execution timeline diverged from SOW baseline through expanded testing phases (PAT, regression) and agile sprint methodology without triggering formal contract amendment process.
triggerConditions: Project activities continue beyond September 11, 2026 contractual end date
Client finance or legal team questions payment milestone applicability beyond contract term
Incident or defect occurs during extended period raising liability questions
Vendor resource commitment uncertainty beyond contractual end date

potentialImpact.legal: Contract breach exposure; ambiguous liability and warranty coverage beyond September 11; potential dispute over acceptance criteria applicability
potentialImpact.financial: Payment milestone delays or withholding; unplanned vendor cost absorption for 49-day extension; potential change order negotiation under duress
potentialImpact.operational: Resource availability uncertainty; deployment approval delays; hypercare support commitment ambiguity

predictedRisks.reasoning: The project is operating 49 days beyond its contractual end date without formal amendment, creating critical legal and commercial risk. Historical evidence shows this exact condition emerged previously when testing phases were added outside the SOW, and weak mitigation allowed the issue to persist. Current evidence confirms PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare activities are planned through October 30, 2026, while the SOW specifies a September 11, 2026 end date. With only 29 days remaining to contractual end and 78 days of planned work, the misalignment is certain to materialize unless immediately addressed.
